This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

candidates: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 - `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.. GNU sed does not accept the separate empty-string backup argument. It reads `''` as the script and the real expression as a file name, so on Linux the command fails and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never replaced. The script then still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL". Fix: use a portable form, such as `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`, or write to a temp file and move it into place.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 - `updateMany` with empty data probably never bumps `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`.. The comment says this updates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every calendar under the credential, but the call passes `{}` as the data. When Prisma gets no fields to set, it skips the write, and `@updatedAt` only fills in when a real update happens. So after a webhook refresh the timestamp most likely stays the same, and anything that reads `updatedAt` to show freshness gets a stale value. I could not check the exact Prisma version's behaviour from here. Fix: set the field explicitly.

packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:89 - Cache timestamp is always formatted in `en-US`, whatever the user's locale.. The "Last updated" string is translated, but the date inside it is always formatted with `"en-US"`. Users with another locale see US month/day ordering and a 12-hour clock, which is confusing in places like the EU, where 07/08 means August 7th. Fix: take the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) and pass it to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.
